newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak opposition fails to sack interior minister.
newsitem.headline: Slovak opposition fails to sack interior minister.

text.p: Slovak opposition deputies failed on Thursday to remove Interior Minister Gustav Krajci for his role in last month's referendum fiasco.
Government parties boycotted the session and the opposition failed to muster a quorum for a vote of no confidence in Krajci.

Krajci removed a proposal for direct presidential elections from the ballot papers distributed by his ministry last month, prompting a widespread boycott which reduced the turnout the less than 10 percent.

The electoral commission refused even to count the votes cast on the remaining questions about Slovakia's wish to join NATO, saying none were valid because of Krajci's last minute change in the ballot.
The dispute was part of a long-running feud between President Michal Kovac and Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar.

The present constitution gives lawmakers the choice of Kovac's successor next March but would allow Meciar to take over presidential powers in a stalemate, which his followers could bring about on their present strength in parliament.
